title: Disconnect bar, reconnect and restore-disconnected
body:
When a Remote Session's ssh exits, keep the Win and show a one-line bar offering reconnect on Enter. Reconnect relaunches the same Remote and directory, with the provider's resume argv for agents, and never resends the original prompt. Persist the Remote name in the workspace snapshot and restore such Sessions disconnected.
Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-20-remote-sessions-design.md (sections: UI > Disconnect, Persistence)
Blocked by: Open a Remote Session from the CLI with --on
Done when:
- a dead ssh leaves the Win in place with the bar; Enter reconnects; other input is ignored
- the resume argv lives in one table; a provider with no entry relaunches fresh
- workspace files without a Remote name load as today; a Terminal with one restores disconnected and opens no connection until Enter
- a Remote name that no longer exists restores as a local Shell with a toast
- snapshot round-trip and the reconnect argv have unit tests
Notes from landed cards:
- The Tunnel (src/control/tunnel.rs) leases one token per connection and revokes it when the Session exits. Reconnect must take a new lease (a fresh Session, or attach_tunnel with a new lease) so the token is renewed and the reply note is sent again on the first chat delivery after the reconnect. Add a test that the old token is refused after a reconnect.
- WindowManager::add_remote_terminal is the one place a Remote Session is spawned today; capture currently saves a Remote Session as a plain local Shell.
- Re-arm the reply note on reconnect through ReplyNote::arm with the same at-launch rule the launch path uses (commit 03761b2); do not add a second note path.
- GUI card: the final report must list the states the human should capture with build-screenshot (the bar on a dead Session, focused and unfocused; a restored-disconnected Session; a narrow Win).
Gate: cargo test --target-dir target/agent workspace; cargo test --target-dir target/agent remote
